items.rationale: Sections 2.4.4 and 7.1.9 cover like-for-like renewal of the internal fitting. Case 25 puts one valve at €51–54 gross.
Section 7.1.9 covers connection elements that must be renewed with the fractured fitting. Case 25 puts one hose at €26–28 gross.
Sections 7.1.7(f) and 7.1.9 cover necessary fitting repair labour. Three hours at €95 gross gives €285, consistent with Case 25.
Sections 3.6 and 7.1.7(e) allow consumables actually used in the repair, but not the contractor’s own small equipment. Allow €7 for repair consumables, consistent with Case 25.
Sections 7.1.9 and 7.1.11 allow one attendance for the covered repair. Case 25 puts the vehicle charge at €38–44 gross.
Sections 2.4.6 and 5.2.2 expressly cover imaging used to trace the escape. Allow €25 for equipment use, consistent with Case 25 and well below the €2,500 gross event cap.
Section 7.1.11 excludes a second attendance by the same undertaking unless approved in advance. No approval is stated; €41 is the conditional estimate if approval is shown.

items.description: Remove loose and spalled facade plaster
items.rationale: The facade frost endorsement and sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(a) cover removal of failed plaster in the damaged area. Allow €40 each for two small removal units, excluding disposal.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) cover like-for-like base plaster for the damaged patches. Allow €45 for material, with labour priced separately.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover necessary substrate reinstatement. Allow €100 for localized work distinct from the base plaster and separately billed painter hours.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) allow priming required by the original finish system in the damaged area. Allow €30 for the separate primer line.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover drying only if needed before repair. If active drying was necessary, allow €75 for a modest localized treatment.
Sections 2.6.2, 7.1.7(d) and 7.1.10 cover only the coats required by a like-for-like finish on the damaged area. Allow €95 gross without assuming all four coats were necessary.
Sections 7.1.7(f) and 7.1.13 allow labour attributable to the frost-damaged elevation, not to the separately billed rear repaint. Five hours at €65 gross gives €325.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.8 cover necessary access for the insured work. At roughly 48 m² and €15/m² gross, allow €720 without apportionment because the rear work used ladders after the scaffold was removed.
Sections 2.6.3(a) and 7.1.5–7.1.6 exclude matching work on a separate undamaged elevation. The positive figure is a conditional pricing placeholder only.
Sections 2.6.2 and 5.2.1 cover disposal of material removed from the insured repair area. Allow €45 gross for transport and disposal of a few rubble sacks, not a skip.
Sections 3.6(b) and 7.1.12 exclude a separately billed administrative fee that prices no repair work. The positive figure is a conditional pricing placeholder only.
Sections 3.6(a) and 7.1.12 exclude crew subsistence even when the repair itself is covered. The €6 figure for all three units is a conditional placeholder consistent with Case 20.
